From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on the cost/TCO questions you raised.

1) Main pain points you described
- High monthly token spend (~3–4B tokens) with unpredictable spikes due to search/chat workloads.
- Latency-sensitive experiences in the support flow (p99 target ~150ms).
- Finance needs a clearer cost model to compare hosted vs dedicated capacity.

2) What we discussed: levers that materially impact cost
- Batching: for your typical burst profile we estimate 20–40% cost savings with 16–32 batch sizes depending on concurrency.
- Prefix / KV caching: customer chat reuse patterns suggest up to 25% token reduction for repeated prompts.
- Model quantization & sharding: Dedicated nodes with int8 quantization can reduce per-token GPU compute costs ~30% (depends on latencies).

3) Rough TCO framing (back-of-envelope) — for your 3.5B tokens/mo baseline
- Hosted (Redwood API): ~$X per 1M tokens (see attached summary) -> estimated $Y/month before discounts.
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs): higher fixed monthly but lower marginal per-token cost; breaks even vs hosted at ~Z tokens/mo and provides stronger latency SLAs.

Attachments: ACME_TCO_v3.xlsx (detailed numbers + sensitivity), redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing and features by deployment mode).

4) Open questions we promised to follow up on
- Exact token mix (prompt vs completion lengths) — if you can share 1-week billing sample, we’ll run a distribution analysis.
- Procurement / timeline constraints — budget window for Q4?
- Compliance/region needs for EU data residency (if applicable to other business units).

Suggested next steps
- Share a 1-week anonymized token/billing sample (CSV) — action: Tom
- We’ll send a calibrated TCO sheet with hosted vs dedicated scenarios by EOD tomorrow — action: Marissa + Naomi
- 30 min follow-up with finance + infra to review numbers and procurement asks — propose Tue 10/28 10:00am PT

Let me know if I missed anything. I’ll upload the workbook now and follow up with a short explainer call invite.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — very clear, appreciate the recap. Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Finance wants a simple line item: cost per 1M tokens (prompt + completion) for hosted vs dedicated (incl. amortized infra). Can you include both list price and expected discounted price at ~commit levels (50%/80% utilization)?
- For batching/caching assumptions — can Naomi include the expected latency impact at p95/p99 when enabling batching for our 150ms p99 requirement? We need both cost and SLA trade-offs.
- Procurement: we have a quarterly budget cap of ~$200k for external AI infra this fiscal year. If Dedicated requires a 12-mo commitment, we need the annualized cost clearly spelled out.

We can share a redacted billing sample next business day. Also looping procurement (procurement@acme.com) so they see the upcoming ask. Can you confirm availability for Tue 10/28 10am PT?

Sara — thanks, and great questions. Quick responses and links below.

1) Cost per 1M tokens (hosted vs dedicated) — high-level numbers included in the attached sheet and the shared Google Sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ACME-TCO-2026
- Hosted list: $0.XX per 1M tokens (prompt+completion)
- Hosted expected w/commit discounts: $0.0Y per 1M tokens at 50% utilization; $0.0Z at 80% utilization
- Dedicated amortized: equivalent to $0.AB per 1M tokens after fixed node costs and expected utilization (assumption = 70% avg).

2) Batching & latency trade-offs
- Small batch sizes (4–8) give modest cost savings (~10–15%) with negligible p99 impact for your profile. Larger batch sizes yield more savings but add 20–40ms p95 and can increase tail latency if concurrency spikes. Naomi will provide a p95/p99 table.

3) Annualized procurement view
- The workbook has a 12-mo committed vs. month-to-month hosted comparison and a breakeven token/month point (see tab "Breakeven"). At your $200k cap, Dedicated becomes attractive if you commit and can guarantee >= Z tokens/mo.

I uploaded ACME_TCO_v3.xlsx and redwood_pricing_summary.pdf to the sheet and added a short notes tab with assumptions (model family, prompt/completion average lengths, batching scenarios).

Next: Naomi and I can join Tue 10/28 10am PT. If procurement wants an alternate time, we can be flexible.

Link to workbook + simplified one-pager for finance: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ACME-TCO-2026
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ACME-2026-Q4-REDWOOD-01

Hi all — adding a quick technical note ahead of Tuesday: 

- For the workload profile you described (short prompts, ~80 token completions, frequent session reuse), our conservative estimate for KV/prefix caching is 18–25% token reduction; we used 20% in the shared sheet.
- If you opt for Dedicated with int8 quantization, we should expect slightly higher variance in p99 during peak compaction windows; we'll propose a canary rollout plan to test on a small shard first.

Happy to walk through the p95/p99 numbers on the call and show a live demo of batching impact on latency.
